glosses: Senses relating to a change of position.
To move (something) from one place or position to another; to transfer.

examples.text: He [John Mackintosh] considers all the eruptions, even erysipelas, in the light of natural blisters, established by powers inherent in the constitution, which enable it to translate disease from the internal organs to the skin; […]

glosses: Senses relating to a change of position.
To move (something) from one place or position to another; to transfer.

examples.text: Consider a collection of objects – perfectly elastic pool balls, perhaps – rattling around inside a closed, isolated container. We can translate the container and its contents through space, and the physics inside the container is unchanged.

glosses: Senses relating to a change of position.
To move (something) from one place or position to another; to transfer.
Of a body: to be subjected to linear motion with no rotation.

examples.text: If the ball were to hit the racket at its center of mass (CM) or balance point (which is usually in the throat of the racket), the racket recoil would be pure translation and there would be no rotation of the racket. Let us assume the gas molecule to be a structureless "billiard ball," translating in space and frequently colliding with the neighboring molecules.

glosses: To entrance (“place in a trance”), to cause to lose recollection or sense.

examples.text: William was translated by the blow to the head he received, being unable to speak for the next few minutes.

glosses: To repair (used shoes, boots or other clothing) for resale.

glosses: In Euclidean spaces: a set of points obtained by adding a given fixed vector to each point of a given set.

examples.text: [F]ractions with a defining relation are nothing but linear orthogonal arrays or their translates.

examples.text: Elle était illettrée, et Jacques ne pouvait lui écrire, car elle n’eût osé montrer à qui que ce soit les lettres de l’officier pour se les faire traduire.

glosses: Transférer d’un lieu à un autre.

examples.text: Quelques mois après la mort du Cardinal Mazarin, on envoya, dans le plus grand secret, au Château de l’Isle Sainte-Marguerite, un prisonnier inconnu. Ce Margnelot a été traduit au châtelet, comme ayant commis un crime de leze-nation; et, depuis treize mois, il est en état de captivité.

glosses: Envoyer quelqu'un devant la justice, afin qu'il soit jugé.
